roles.summary: Owns the weekly production sequence for two to three lines per plant, today built by hand in Excel from an MRP extract and defended by phone. Under ERP the plan is generated by the system and the scheduler's job becomes validating it, clearing exceptions and releasing orders inside rules that no longer bend to local judgement.
before: Builds the weekly plan in Excel from an MRP extract
Negotiates line changes by phone
Owns sequencing on local judgement
Reconciles variances by hand at week end
after: Plan is system-generated
Scheduler validates and clears exceptions
Releases orders in-system
Sequencing constrained by system rules
Every change carries a reason code
constraints: Sequencing authority moves from local judgement to rules-based exception approval
6 plants, each with its own local sequencing conventions
Plants go live in waves, not simultaneously

roles.summary: Runs a shift team of pickers and forklift drivers across the two DCs and the six plant warehouses, coordinating by radio against paper pick lists and absorbing exceptions with local workarounds. ERP replaces paper with handheld scanning and real-time confirmation, so the shift's work becomes visible as it happens instead of being typed up at the end of it.
before: Paper pick lists
Radio coordination
Local workarounds absorb exceptions
Nothing enters the system until end of shift
after: Handheld scanning
Real-time confirmation
System-directed putaway
No retrospective entry
constraints: Deskless
3 shifts
No corporate email
4 languages across sites
2 prior failed WMS attempts

roles.summary: Processes supplier invoices for the whole group, today keying from PDFs and chasing mismatches by email against a shared mailbox. ERP introduces three-way match and automated posting, so the routine invoice disappears from the desk entirely and the remaining work is exception resolution the specialist no longer has discretion to override.
before: Keys invoices manually from PDF and paper into the finance system
Chases purchase order and receipt mismatches by email
Holds and releases payment blocks on personal judgement
Maintains a private spreadsheet of supplier quirks and payment terms
Builds the weekly payment run by hand
after: Reviews invoices captured by OCR into the ERP workflow
Works only the exceptions that fail three-way match
Escalates blocks through system-defined approval rules
Supplier terms read from validated master data, not local notes
Payment proposal generated by the system and reviewed, not built
constraints: Shared-mailbox working practice disappears at go-live
Blocking and releasing payment moves from personal judgement to rules
Month-end close window cannot slip

roles.summary: A role that does not exist today: material, customer, vendor and BOM records are currently maintained by whoever needs them, in whichever system. The stewards become the single gate for creating and changing master data company-wide, which means designing governance while learning the tooling that enforces it.
before: No role exists; records are created ad hoc by requesters in each function
Material and customer data duplicated across four legacy systems
Data quality fixed reactively after a transaction fails
No owner for definitions, naming conventions or approval routes
after: Owns create, change and block requests for all master data domains
Runs the governed workflow with mandatory field and duplicate checks
Publishes and enforces naming and classification standards
Monitors data-quality dashboards and drives correction at source
Trains and audits requesters company-wide
constraints: Net new headcount - 18 people to recruit or redeploy before go-live
Blocking role: every downstream process depends on it from day one
No incumbent knowledge to build training on

roles.summary: The largest single affected population: order takers across three service centres who currently type orders from email, phone and fax into a legacy order system and fix pricing by hand. ERP validates credit, pricing and availability at entry, so orders that used to be forced through now stop and have to be resolved.
before: Keys orders from email, phone and fax into the legacy order system
Looks up price and discount in a shared spreadsheet
Overrides credit holds after a phone call to the account manager
Confirms availability by calling the DC
Re-keys amendments as new orders
after: Enters or reviews orders in ERP with validation at point of entry
Pricing and discount applied automatically from condition records
Credit block resolution follows a system workflow, no verbal override
Real-time availability check replaces the call to the DC
Amends the original order rather than re-keying it
Answers customer queries from live order status
constraints: 3 service centres on different shift patterns
Highest ticket volume predicted at go-live - hypercare sizing driver
Peak season overlaps the second deployment wave

roles.summary: One controller plus a small team per plant, today rebuilding cost and variance reporting in Excel every month from extracts because the ledger cannot answer the question locally. ERP gives real-time actual costing and standard variance reporting, which removes the rebuild but exposes the plant's numbers continuously rather than once a month.
before: Rebuilds the plant cost report in Excel each month from ledger extracts
Calculates production variances manually against local standards
Maintains a shadow set of cost centres and allocation rules
Explains the gap between plant numbers and corporate numbers
Prepares month-end accruals from emailed input
after: Reviews standard variance reporting generated in-system
Analyses actual costing in real time rather than reconstructing it
Works from one governed cost centre and allocation structure
Plant and corporate report from the same ledger, so the gap conversation ends
Accruals raised through workflow with system-held audit trail
constraints: Month-end close timetable compresses from 8 days to 4
Shadow Excel cost model is decommissioned, not migrated
roles.deckNote: Deck slide 10 prints adoption risk 3.6 for this role while labelling it Enable, which is self-contradictory under the stated 3.5 threshold. This dataset uses 3.4 so the quadrant rule holds and the deck's Enable label is preserved.

roles.summary: Buys indirect materials, spares and local services for a single plant, today with wide discretion over supplier choice and a phone relationship with the maintenance team. ERP routes demand through catalogues and approval limits, so the buyer's autonomy over who gets the order narrows sharply even though the daily volume barely changes.
before: Raises purchase orders in the legacy system from emailed requests
Chooses suppliers on local relationship and availability
Expedites by phone and updates requesters verbally
Keeps local price lists and informal agreements outside any system
Approves low-value spend at own discretion
after: Converts system-generated requisitions into POs within release strategy
Buys against group contracts and catalogues where they exist
Expedites via system-flagged confirmation dates and documented follow-up
Local agreements captured as contracts in master data or they do not exist
Approval limits enforced by the system, not by custom
constraints: Decision rights on supplier selection move to category management
6 plants with 6 different local supplier bases
Maintenance downtime pressure makes off-catalogue buying the default habit

roles.summary: Sets and polices customer credit limits and chases overdue cash, today from a downloaded aged-debt report and a personal call list. ERP scores credit automatically, blocks orders in real time and drives a worklist, which turns judgement-led collection into exception handling against system rules.
before: Downloads aged debt to Excel and builds a personal call list
Sets and releases credit limits on judgement and history
Releases blocked orders informally when sales pushes
Applies cash to invoices manually from bank statements
Reports collection status in a weekly slide pack
after: Works a system-generated collections worklist with dunning levels
Credit limits derived from scoring rules and reviewed, not invented
Order release follows documented workflow with recorded reason codes
Cash application largely automated; analyst clears unmatched residuals
Reports from live receivables dashboards
constraints: Credit release authority becomes rule-based and auditable
Sales relationships built on informal release will feel the change first

roles.summary: Builds the rolling 18-month forecast per category, today in a spreadsheet model owned personally and reconciled with sales by negotiation. ERP demand planning replaces the private model with a statistical baseline plus a governed consensus process, so overrides become visible and must be justified.
before: Maintains a personal Excel forecast model per category
Collects sales input by email and merges it manually
Adjusts the forecast on judgement without recording why
Reconciles against supply constraints in a separate spreadsheet
Publishes the forecast as a monthly file
after: Reviews a statistical baseline generated in the planning module
Runs consensus review in-system with sales input captured as entries
Every override carries a reason code and is measured for bias
Constrained plan produced by the system, not stitched together
Forecast is live master data consumed downstream, not a file
constraints: Forecast override discretion becomes measured and reviewable
Requires statistical-forecasting literacy the current team does not have

roles.summary: The HR front door at each plant: paper starters, time-sheet corrections, absence records and shift allowances handled locally and often on trust. ERP and its self-service layer move most of that to employees and line managers, leaving the coordinator to administer exceptions and police data quality for a deskless workforce.
before: Collects paper starter, leaver and change forms and re-keys them
Corrects clocking errors on behalf of operators
Maintains local absence and shift allowance spreadsheets
Answers pay queries by calling central payroll
Keeps the plant training matrix in Excel
after: Guides employees and line managers through self-service transactions
Approves time and attendance exceptions in the ERP workflow
Absence and allowances held once, in the system of record
Resolves pay queries from live employee data
Maintains qualifications in the ERP training record
constraints: Deskless population with no corporate email must be onboarded to self-service
3 shifts - coordinators cover only day shift
Works councils consulted per site on time-recording change

roles.summary: The route-to-market force calling on independent and wholesale accounts, today taking orders on paper or by phone into customer service and quoting price from memory. ERP-backed mobile order capture puts validated pricing, credit status and stock in their hands, which removes the paperwork but also removes the room to promise what the system will not allow.
before: Writes orders on a pad and phones or emails them to customer service
Quotes price and promotion from a printed list and memory
Has no visibility of the customer's credit or payment status
Reports calls and competitor activity in a weekly spreadsheet
Chases delivery status through the service centre
after: Captures the order on a mobile device with live validation
Prices from live condition records, including promotion eligibility
Sees credit status and open items before promising a delivery
Call reporting captured in-app as part of the visit
Reads order and delivery status directly, no service-centre call
constraints: 4 sales regions with different journey plans
Mobile coverage gaps require offline order capture
Bonus scheme tied to order volume - any friction is felt as pay risk

roles.summary: Handles deductions, damages, shortages and returns across the three service centres, today reconstructing each case from emails, proof-of-delivery scans and phone calls. ERP gives a structured returns and claims process with linked documents, so cases follow a defined path with a documented settlement authority.
before: Reconstructs each claim from an email trail and scanned paperwork
Raises credit notes in the legacy system with free-text justification
Tracks open cases in a team spreadsheet
Agrees goodwill settlements verbally with the account manager
Arranges returns collection by phone with the DC
after: Logs claims as structured cases linked to the original order and delivery
Credit notes generated from the case with mandatory reason coding
Case status, ageing and ownership visible in-system
Settlement values fall inside system-held authority thresholds
Returns orders trigger DC receipt and inspection automatically
constraints: 3 service centres with different local claim conventions
Goodwill authority becomes a system threshold rather than a conversation

roles.summary: Bills customers and maintains the receivables ledger, today running billing in batches and correcting invoices after issue. ERP bills from the delivery automatically and closes most of the manual correction loop, moving the work to control and dispute support.
before: Creates invoices in batches from delivery paperwork
Corrects and reissues invoices after customer complaint
Reconciles the sub-ledger to the general ledger in Excel
Files invoice copies and proof of delivery manually
Answers customer statement requests by hand
after: Billing runs automatically from confirmed deliveries
Investigates billing blocks before the invoice is issued
Sub-ledger reconciles continuously against the general ledger
Invoice and delivery documents held and retrieved in-system
Statements and account histories self-generated
constraints: Invoice accuracy at go-live drives customer-facing risk
Legacy billing corrections cannot be migrated

roles.summary: Maintains price lists, promotional terms and trade allowances, today across spreadsheets issued to sales and customer service by email. ERP holds pricing as governed condition records with validity dates and approval, which makes every commercial term explicit and auditable.
before: Maintains price and promotion lists in Excel and emails them out
Applies customer-specific deals as manual overrides at order entry
Tracks accrued trade spend in a separate workbook
Reconciles claimed against agreed allowances after the fact
Answers 'what is the right price' questions ad hoc
after: Maintains pricing as condition records with validity periods
Customer deals modelled as agreements, applied automatically
Trade spend accrues in-system as orders are priced
Claims validated against the recorded agreement, not memory
Pricing enquiries answered from the single source of record
constraints: Every legacy special price must be cleansed and re-created before go-live
Pricing errors are immediately customer-visible

roles.summary: Owns supplier strategy and negotiation for a spend category, today with contracts held as documents and compliance measured retrospectively from spend reports. ERP makes contracts operational objects that route demand, so the category manager gains real control but also owns the data that enforces it.
before: Negotiates and stores contracts as documents on a shared drive
Measures compliance retrospectively from spend extracts
Communicates preferred suppliers by email and slide deck
Tracks savings in a personal tracker
Handles escalations from plants by phone
after: Loads contracts as ERP agreements with pricing and release rules
Sees off-contract buying as it happens, not months later
Catalogue and source list steer demand automatically
Savings measured against system-held baselines
Plant escalations arrive as workflow items with context attached
constraints: Gains decision rights that plant buyers currently hold
Contract data quality is now the control, so it becomes their job

roles.summary: Processes non-production purchasing for HQ and commercial functions, today from emailed requests and a lot of chasing. ERP self-service requisitioning pushes request creation to the requester and leaves the buyer sourcing the exceptions.
before: Receives purchase requests by email and re-keys them as orders
Chases approvals by walking the floor and calling managers
Sources ad hoc from search engines and past invoices
Tracks order status in a personal spreadsheet
Fields 'where is my order' calls all day
after: Reviews requisitions raised by requesters in self-service
Approvals route automatically through release strategy
Sources against catalogues and contracts first, ad hoc by exception
Order status visible to requesters without asking
Focuses on sourcing the exceptions and onboarding suppliers
constraints: Requesters across HQ must be trained on self-service requisitioning
Volume of low-value orders drops sharply, changing the job shape

roles.summary: Balances demand against plant capacity and inventory targets for a portfolio of SKUs, today by exporting to a spreadsheet model and negotiating with plants. ERP runs constrained supply planning centrally, so planning becomes exception management against parameters the planner now owns.
before: Exports demand and stock to a spreadsheet supply model
Sets safety stock by rule of thumb per SKU family
Negotiates plant allocation by phone and email
Rebuilds the deployment plan weekly by hand
Explains stock-outs after they happen
after: Reviews constrained supply proposals generated in-system
Maintains planning parameters that the system then applies
Allocation follows recorded priority rules across plants
Deployment and replenishment proposals generated automatically
Acts on forward-looking shortage alerts, not post-mortems
constraints: Planning parameter maintenance is new and unglamorous but load-bearing
Requires trust in a plan the planner did not build by hand

roles.summary: Keeps the plant's stock record honest: cycle counts, write-offs, stock in quality hold and the endless reconciliation of the system against the racking. ERP moves inventory in real time from scanned transactions, so the reconciliation shrinks but discrepancies surface immediately and publicly.
before: Reconciles system stock to physical counts in Excel
Posts adjustments in batches with limited documentation
Tracks quality-hold stock on a whiteboard
Investigates discrepancies days or weeks after they occur
Runs an annual wall-to-wall count as the real control
after: Manages cycle counting scheduled and recorded in-system
Adjustments posted with mandatory reason codes and approval limits
Quality status held on the batch, not on a board
Investigates discrepancies the day the scan creates them
Continuous accuracy metric replaces the annual count as the control
constraints: Stock accuracy at cutover determines whether the plant can ship
6 plants with materially different current count discipline

roles.summary: Plans preventive and corrective maintenance per plant, today from a standalone CMMS and a paper job card culture. ERP brings maintenance orders, spares reservation and cost capture into the same system as production, linking the plan to line availability for the first time.
before: Plans work orders in a standalone maintenance system
Issues paper job cards and collects them back partially completed
Requests spares by walking to the stores counter
Estimates job duration from experience, unrecorded
Reports compliance by counting job cards
after: Plans maintenance orders in ERP against production scheduling
Technicians confirm work and time against the order digitally
Spares reserved and issued against the order automatically
Task lists hold standard durations and materials
Compliance and cost reported from the order data
constraints: Depends on technicians confirming work digitally - a deskless dependency
Legacy CMMS history is not fully migrated

roles.summary: Runs the corporate close: journals, intercompany, accruals and reconciliations, today across three ledgers with a manual consolidation on top. ERP delivers a single ledger with continuous reconciliation, which compresses the close and eliminates most of the manual journal work.
before: Posts manual journals from emailed templates
Consolidates three legacy ledgers in a spreadsheet
Reconciles balance sheet accounts monthly by hand
Chases intercompany differences by email
Builds the reporting pack from extracts
after: Reviews journals raised through workflow with attachments and approval
Reports from a single ledger - no consolidation spreadsheet
Uses in-system account reconciliation with continuous status
Intercompany matched and eliminated automatically
Reporting pack generated from live ledger data
constraints: Close timetable compresses from 8 days to 4
Statutory and audit requirements leave no tolerance for cutover error

roles.summary: Produces budgets, forecasts and management reporting, today by pulling extracts into a large Excel model. ERP-integrated planning removes most of the extract-and-rebuild cycle; the analytical judgement is unchanged but the plumbing under it is entirely new.
before: Pulls monthly extracts into a master Excel reporting model
Chases cost centre owners for commentary by email
Rebuilds the forecast template each cycle
Reconciles reported numbers against the ledger by hand
Distributes reporting as attachments
after: Reports from integrated planning data with drill-down to the ledger
Commentary captured in the planning application against the variance
Forecast templates are configured once and reused
Reporting ties to the ledger by construction
Stakeholders self-serve dashboards instead of receiving files
constraints: Excel model ownership is a source of personal status, not just a tool
Reporting definitions must be agreed before they can be configured

roles.summary: The central HR service desk for hires, changes, leavers and contract administration, today driven by forms and a case mailbox. ERP self-service and workflow move initiation to managers and employees, leaving the specialist to handle exceptions and govern the data.
before: Receives change requests as email forms and re-keys them
Manages cases in a shared mailbox with no status visibility
Produces contracts and letters from Word templates by hand
Maintains organisational structure in a drawing tool
Compiles headcount reporting manually each month
after: Reviews manager-initiated transactions in the ERP workflow
Works a ticketed queue with visible status and service levels
Generates documents from templates driven by system data
Maintains the organisational structure as live master data
Headcount reporting available on demand from the same structure
constraints: Manager self-service adoption determines whether volume actually shifts
Data privacy rules constrain who can see what in the new authorisation model

roles.summary: Runs the monthly and weekly payrolls, today assembling inputs from plant spreadsheets and correcting after the fact. ERP integrates time and attendance directly into payroll, which removes the manual assembly but makes upstream data errors visible as pay errors immediately.
before: Collects time and allowance inputs from plant spreadsheets
Keys adjustments and retro corrections by hand
Runs pre-payroll checks against printed reports
Issues corrections in the following period
Answers pay queries by rebuilding the calculation manually
after: Payroll draws time and absence data directly from the ERP record
Adjustments entered once, in-system, with audit trail
Runs simulation and validation reports before committing
Errors caught in-period through pre-payroll controls
Pay queries answered from the system's own calculation trace
constraints: Zero tolerance for pay error - the single most reputationally sensitive cutover
Depends on plant time-recording data being clean on day one

roles.summary: Picks, packs and puts away stock in the two distribution centres. The physical work is unchanged, but the paper list and the end-of-shift keying are replaced by a handheld that directs and records every move - and the population has watched two WMS attempts fail already.
before: Picks against a printed pick list and marks it by hand
Puts away wherever there is space and remembers where
Reports shortages verbally to the team lead
Paperwork is keyed by someone else after the shift
after: Picks against handheld instructions and scans each confirmation
Puts away where the system directs
Records shortages on the device at the point of discovery
No after-the-fact keying - the shift's record is complete when it ends
constraints: Deskless
No corporate email
3 shifts
4 languages across sites
2 prior failed WMS attempts
Significant agency and seasonal workforce

roles.summary: Fixes and services production equipment across the six plants. The engineering work does not change; what changes is that every job, every hour and every spare part must be confirmed against a maintenance order on a shared terminal instead of on a job card.
before: Receives work as a paper job card or a verbal request
Draws spares from stores against a signature
Writes up what was done, sometimes, at end of shift
Keeps personal knowledge of each machine's history
after: Receives work as a maintenance order on a shop-floor terminal
Spares issued against the order, updating stock in real time
Confirms time and findings against the order before closing it
Machine history accumulates in the system for everyone to use
constraints: Deskless
No corporate email
3 shifts
Shared terminals only - no personal device
Long-tenure workforce, low prior system exposure

roles.summary: Moves raw materials, WIP and finished pallets between stores, lines and despatch inside the plants. The routes and the truck are the same; the difference is that each movement is now scanned and the system, not the driver, decides where the pallet goes.
before: Moves pallets on verbal instruction from the line or team lead
Records nothing, or writes on the pallet label
Decides storage location from experience
Line-side shortages resolved by walking to stores
after: Receives transfer instructions on a truck-mounted or handheld device
Scans every pallet movement as it happens
Puts away and picks where the system directs
Line replenishment triggered by system signal, not a shout
constraints: Deskless
No corporate email
3 shifts
Device must be usable with gloves in a cold store
Mixed literacy and 4 languages across sites

roles.summary: Runs a production shift: people, safety, output and the hundred small decisions that keep the line running. Most of that is untouched, but overtime, absence and time corrections move into system workflow with limits attached - so what changes is authority, not workload.
before: Approves overtime and shift swaps verbally on the floor
Corrects clocking data on a paper sheet sent to HR
Records absence in a shift book
Signs off production output on a paper log
Manages the line plan from a printed schedule
after: Approves overtime and absence in workflow, inside system-held limits
Time corrections entered once, in-system, with reason codes
Absence recorded against the employee record as it happens
Confirms production output in-system during the shift
Works from the live schedule, with changes visible immediately
constraints: Deskless
3 shifts
No corporate email for most of the population
Approval authority becomes a system limit rather than a judgement call
340 supervisors group-wide need the decision-rights briefing

roles.summary: Samples, tests and releases product at each plant. The tests are unchanged and the standards are unchanged; the batch record, the hold and the release decision move from a lab logbook into the system, where the hold is visible to everybody instantly.
before: Records test results in a lab logbook and a local spreadsheet
Communicates holds and releases by phone and printed label
Assembles the batch record from paper at the end of the run
Tracks retests and deviations locally
after: Enters results against the inspection lot in-system
Usage decision in the system sets stock status automatically
Batch record assembled continuously from system data
Deviations and retests recorded as structured, reportable events
constraints: Deskless for part of the shift; shared lab terminals
Regulatory and customer-audit exposure on batch records
Release authority becomes a system status, visible group-wide

roles.summary: Owns the relationship and the P&L for a major retail customer. The commercial job is unchanged, but the discretion to promise a price, a delivery date or a goodwill credit is replaced by system-held agreements and thresholds - which is exactly the part they value most.
before: Agrees prices and promotions directly with the customer, then tells the business
Promises delivery dates based on relationships in the plant and DC
Approves goodwill credits verbally with customer service
Tracks account performance in a personal spreadsheet
after: Commercial terms recorded as agreements before they are quotable
Delivery promises come from system availability, not a favour
Goodwill sits inside a system-held approval threshold
Account performance read from live customer reporting
constraints: Decision rights on price, date and goodwill all narrow at once
Highest-influence population - resistance here is contagious
Bonus tied to account P&L they no longer fully control

roles.summary: Manages a field sales region and its targets. Day-to-day tasks barely change, but discount approval and forecast overrides become system-recorded, and the team's activity becomes visible in a way it never was.
before: Approves discounts and exceptions verbally or by email
Builds the regional forecast from reps' spreadsheets
Reviews performance from a monthly reporting pack
Manages coverage from local knowledge
after: Approves discounts in workflow within recorded authority limits
Regional forecast aggregates in-system from captured rep input
Reviews live regional dashboards instead of a monthly pack
Coverage and call compliance visible from captured activity
constraints: Discount authority becomes explicit and logged
Team performance becomes transparent upward as well as downward

roles.summary: Receives inbound materials at the plant gate. The physical check is the same; the difference is that receipt is now scanned against the purchase order in real time, and short or over-deliveries can no longer be smoothed over with the supplier informally.
before: Signs the supplier's delivery note and files a copy
Keys receipts into the legacy system in a batch later
Resolves quantity differences directly with the driver or supplier
Passes paperwork to AP by internal post
after: Scans receipt against the purchase order at the point of delivery
Stock and PO status update in real time, no batch keying
Differences raised as system discrepancies routed to the buyer
No paperwork handoff - the document flow is automatic
constraints: Deskless
No corporate email
Shared gatehouse terminal
Blocks AP invoice matching if receipts are late or wrong

roles.summary: Builds loads and books carriers out of the two DCs. The task list is broadly the same, but load building and paperwork are system-driven, and the coordinator loses the ability to reshuffle a load informally once it is released.
before: Builds loads from a printed pick and ship list
Books carriers by phone and records it on a whiteboard
Produces delivery paperwork from a local template
Adjusts loads verbally with the warehouse team lead
after: Builds and releases deliveries and shipments in-system
Carrier and route assigned from system-held transport data
Delivery documents printed from the shipment record
Load changes require a system change with a reason code
constraints: Carrier cut-off times leave no slack for system learning at go-live
Informal load reshuffling with the floor stops working

roles.summary: Advises plant leadership on people matters. The advisory work is unchanged, but headcount, absence and performance data become transparent group-wide, and the site loses the ability to manage its numbers privately.
before: Reports site headcount and absence from a local spreadsheet
Runs performance and case management on local records
Advises managers on process from experience and local precedent
Negotiates local practice variations informally
after: Site data visible group-wide from the same live record
Cases and performance recorded in the system of record
Advises managers through the standard, system-enforced process
Local variations must be configured or they cease to exist
constraints: Site autonomy over people data ends
Change fatigue at plant level is already high
Must sponsor the deskless self-service rollout without owning it

roles.summary: Accountable for the whole plant. Few of their own tasks change, but almost every decision right they delegate downward is redefined at once, and their site's performance becomes continuously visible to the centre.
before: Runs the plant on locally defined KPIs and reporting
Delegates approval authority by custom and trust
Reports performance to the centre monthly, with narrative
Approves capital and spend requests on paper
after: Reports on group-standard KPIs from the same live data as the centre
Delegates through configured authorisation and release strategies
Performance visible continuously; the monthly narrative loses its role
Approvals arrive and are recorded in workflow
constraints: Sponsorship role - their visible behaviour sets site adoption
Loses the ability to shape the story before the centre sees the numbers

roles.summary: Runs and changes over the production and packing lines across the six plants - by far the largest single population. The work itself is untouched; the only difference is that output and downtime confirmation happens on a line terminal that a team lead usually drives.
before: Runs the line to a printed schedule at the line head
Records output and downtime on a paper log
Reports issues verbally to the team lead
Draws components from a line-side supermarket without recording it
after: Runs the line to the schedule shown on the line terminal
Output and downtime confirmed at the terminal during the shift
Issues raised as system-visible events by the team lead
Component consumption backflushed automatically from confirmation
constraints: Deskless
No corporate email
3 shifts
4 languages across sites
Broadcast comms must reach them via shift huddle and QR code, not email

roles.summary: Works the shelf in grocery and convenience stores - facings, displays, planogram compliance. They do not transact in ERP at all; the only visible change is that the product and pack data behind their existing field app becomes governed master data.
before: Completes store visits against a printed call list
Reports compliance and stock gaps in the existing field app
Flags out-of-stocks to the account manager by phone
Uses printed planograms and product sheets
after: Same call cycle and same field app
Product and pack data in the app comes from governed master data
Out-of-stock flags reach the account team faster through the same route
Planogram and product references stay current because the source is single
constraints: Deskless
No corporate email
Part-time and territory-based
Comms must land through the field app, not the intranet

roles.summary: Runs brand plans, campaigns and NPD launches. Their daily work sits outside the ERP, but launch dates, pack data and promotional terms now have to be committed into governed processes with lead times they cannot shortcut.
before: Briefs new packs and promotions by email and slide deck
Sets launch dates commercially and expects supply to follow
Tracks campaign spend in agency and finance spreadsheets
Requests product codes from whoever can create one
after: Briefs launches through the governed NPD and master-data process
Launch dates respect system-held material creation and planning lead times
Campaign spend visible against purchase orders and accruals
Product codes requested from the Master Data Steward with defined lead time
constraints: Broadcast comms only; the real dependency is respecting master-data lead times

roles.summary: Develops recipes, packs and specifications. Laboratory and development work is unaffected, but the handover point changes: recipes and bills of material become structured ERP objects created through master-data governance rather than emailed as documents.
before: Maintains recipes and specifications in development documents
Emails the bill of material to the plant at handover
Iterates pack and component data informally with suppliers
Tracks trials in project spreadsheets
after: Recipes and BOMs handed over as structured master-data requests
Plant consumes the same BOM the developer specified, with no re-keying
Component and packaging data validated against vendor master
Trial materials and costs visible in the same system as production
constraints: Broadcast comms only, plus a short briefing on the master-data handover route
